tips.title: Scribing Panel Lines with RB Productions Tools
tips.text: To achieve crisp panel lines, use RB Productions scribing tools. They have interchangeable blades and allow for adjustable depth. For ICM kits, start with the deepest blade (0.2mm) for heavy panel lines, then use progressively shallower blades (0.15mm, 0.1mm) for fine details. Apply gentle pressure, moving the tool parallel to the panel line. Always test on scrap parts first.

tips.title: Airbrush Needle Cleaning Technique
tips.text: Clean your Iwata airbrush needle regularly with Vallejo Airbrush Thinner and a soft brush. For stubborn paint buildup, use a dental pick to scrape gently. Never use pins or needles to clean the needle, as they can damage it. After cleaning, blow air through the needle to ensure it's clear.

tips.title: Masking with Tamiya Tape vs Kabuki Tape
tips.text: Tamiya tape is great for general use, but for complex shapes and fine details, use Kabuki tape. Kabuki tape has a more flexible backing and adheres better to curves. For masking large areas, use Tamiya tape; for intricate details, use Kabuki tape. Always test adhesion on scrap parts first.

tips.title: Progression with Sanding Sticks
tips.text: For smooth surfaces, use sanding sticks in progressive grits starting from coarse to fine. Begin by lightly sanding along the panel lines with the coarse grit, then follow up with medium and fine grits. Sand in the direction of the panel lines to avoid visible scratches. Use light pressure and regular sandpaper, not foam sticks.

tips.title: Scratch-Building with Evergreen Styrene Sheet
tips.text: Evergreen styrene sheet is perfect for scratch-building details. To create a simple antenna, draw the shape on the sheet, then use a sharp hobby knife and a metal ruler to cut it out. Round off sharp corners with a fine file or sandpaper. Use Tamiya Extra Thin Cement to attach it to the model. For complex shapes, use a combination of cutting, bending, and gluing.
